Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates multiple well-defined pulmonary nodules of varying sizes (some up to 3 cm) that are predominantly located in the lower lung zones, with no obvious calcification. This specific radiographic pattern is characteristic of necrotizing sarcoid granulomatosis, distinguishing it from the upper-zone predominance of tuberculosis or the uniform distribution of typical sarcoidosis.
